replies.body: I understand, in my mind the sounds are retro and there is a volume slider in the top right, sorry if it's not clearly visible

replies.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
replies.body: Of course, it is your design. It has potential to be a popular satisfying "relaxation" type of games IMO with the right touches

replies.author: Consistent_Reveal_53
replies.body: I'm always open to suggestions bro

replies.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
replies.body:
I think you are on to something with the plant clipping mechanic. Personally i would focus exclusively on that and make it more visceral/relaxing, particularly the sound effects and music. Not really have lives, but give a percentage of completion after it's done. But yeah take these with a grain of salt, these things are subjective, it's your vision.

What did you use to make this btw if you don't mind me asking?

replies.author: Consistent_Reveal_53
replies.body:
I agree with your vision actually, this one is specifically time based for the 20 seconds jam, as a new project your vision is good,

what did I used to make this? Surprise Surprise Claude code for everything apart from Nora which I made with Grok, the trick is to make it good enough to not be slop.

replies.author: Illustrious-Lime-863
replies.body: Yeah I know what you mean. I've been experimenting with Cline on VS Code (various models), and with Antigravity but that gets throttled quickly. You can definitely already do something playable and non-sloppy if you put some work and polish into it, some quality back and forth. Keep going! These technologies will bring out a lot of creative potential to people like you, don't let the deniers and the haters discourage you. It's the worst they will ever be, will only get better from here.
